title: Pride of Craft Is Unequaled Pride
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Using the handcrafted shoemaking process at Cole Haan as its case study, this piece argues that loyalty and engagement flow from ownership of craft rather than from perks or company culture initiatives. Because a single artisan sees each shoe through the entire production process, workers develop deep pride in the finished product, which the author connects to unusually low turnover in an industry with plenty of nearby competitors. The broader lesson for leaders is that giving team members end-to-end ownership over a product or service builds the kind of pride that translates directly into engagement, quality, and loyalty.
points: Cole Haan artisans each see a shoe through the entire handcrafted production process, from cutting to boxing.
That ownership over the finished product is credited with unusually low turnover in the shoemaking trade.
Pride of ownership, more than benefits or company loyalty programs, drives engagement and quality.
Giving team members full control over what they create builds gratification that translates into retention.
quotes: Each pair of Cole Haan shoes takes five craftsmen up to 30 hours to produce by hand.
The reason is not how special the company is or the benefits offered to the team.
Those who own the work take the utmost pride in the outcome.
Great leaders know that loyalty springs from the pride of controlling the quality of the products or services being created.
An organization or team filled with people proud of the work they do will stand firm against adversity and challenge.
